title: Contract coverage discovered after repair
source_story: User-provided fictional owner stories in this conversation; opening narrative below is a faithful condensed adaptation, not a verbatim transcript.
business_context: 18 staff; approximately 110 mixed PC, printer and network maintenance customers.
owner_narrative: We dispatch when the customer is under contract, but that does not mean the device or work is covered. A personal laptop was repaired at an office, and a part replacement was waived because nobody warned the customer about the charge. Lists are outdated.

diagnostic_interview.question: Is coverage organization-wide or asset-specific?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Both exist, depending on the agreement.
diagnostic_interview.diagnostic_value: A customer match alone is insufficient.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: An unlisted device may be covered by a site-wide agreement; never classify it as excluded solely because the asset list is incomplete.

diagnostic_interview.question: Who authorizes out-of-scope work?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Some site contacts may approve labor but not parts.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

diagnostic_interview.question: Do technicians know a device is unlisted?
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

diagnostic_interview.question: Can goodwill exceptions be made?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: The owner allows small exceptions but records no reason.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

evidence.description: A simulated device record identifies personal ownership.
A simulated contract excludes replacement parts.
A simulated work report contains no charge approval.

diagnoses.hypothesis: Coverage decisions occur after irreversible work because scope and approval authority are not available at the point of service.
diagnoses.counterhypothesis: An unlisted device may be covered by a site-wide agreement; never classify it as excluded solely because the asset list is incomplete.
diagnoses.confidence_policy: Qualitative case-world support only; requires fresh customer evidence before reuse.

interventions.process_first: Define covered, excluded and uncertain states; provide a pre-work approval path and documented goodwill authority.
interventions.deterministic_and_assisted_automation: Retrieve the effective agreement and asset scope; surface coverage evidence; create approval requests when scope changes.
interventions.rejected_default: Do not replace the whole service platform or deploy autonomous agents solely because the owner reports inefficiency.
interventions.selection_basis: Choose the least complex intervention addressing the supported handoff failure; compare added administration and integration burden.

requirements.statement: Uncertain coverage cannot silently become a billable authorization.
requirements.rationale: Coverage decisions occur after irreversible work because scope and approval authority are not available at the point of service.

requirements.statement: Approval binds to amount, scope and version.
requirements.rationale: Coverage decisions occur after irreversible work because scope and approval authority are not available at the point of service.

requirements.statement: A scope change invalidates an inadequate prior approval.
requirements.rationale: Coverage decisions occur after irreversible work because scope and approval authority are not available at the point of service.

requirements.statement: Goodwill is recorded separately from contractual inclusion.
requirements.rationale: Coverage decisions occur after irreversible work because scope and approval authority are not available at the point of service.

acceptance_tests.scenario_and_expected_result: A site-wide contract can cover a newly added device after review.
A higher-cost replacement requires renewed approval.

capability_boundary.proposed_extension: Effective-dated coverage checks and approval controls are new capabilities.
capability_boundary.pricing: No price assigned; current rate card must not be extended by analogy.

evaluation.primary_metric_definition: Chargeable jobs with valid pre-work authorization / chargeable jobs; track waived charges and approval delay.
measurement_cautions: Use a stable denominator and comparable operating periods.
Record missingness and changed case mix.
Do not infer staff reductions from reclaimed task minutes.

implementation.baseline: Collect at least one representative operating cycle before rollout; for monthly billing or maintenance include the relevant full cycle. Extend sampling when volumes or seasonality make the sample unrepresentative.
implementation.scope: Start with one consenting customer group and the staff who own its handoffs; include a normal case and each listed exception.
sequence: Reconcile identities and existing obligations with the process owner.
Run the proposed rules in shadow mode; record disagreements and missed exceptions.
Approve a bounded live pilot only after requirements and exceptions have named owners.
Review outcome metrics, added administrative work and failure logs before expanding.
implementation.simulated_resolution: In this fictional case, MILO introduced the process change: Define covered, excluded and uncertain states; provide a pre-work approval path and documented goodwill authority. The team adopted the proposed workflow for the pilot scope. Routine coordination became explicit; unresolved exceptions continued to require a person.
implementation.simulated_lesson: An unlisted device may be covered by a site-wide agreement; never classify it as excluded solely because the asset list is incomplete.
implementation.rollback: Pause automated writes and notifications, retain the event log, export outstanding work and return to a named manual coordinator. Reconcile queued events before resuming to avoid duplicate actions.
implementation.go_no_go: Process owner reviews coverage of acceptance cases, unresolved critical failures, metric direction and staff workload. No fixed performance threshold is claimed without customer agreement.

open_questions: Spending limits and contract interpretation require owner confirmation.

transfer_rules.applicable_when: Coverage decisions occur after irreversible work because scope and approval authority are not available at the point of service.
transfer_rules.do_not_assume: An unlisted device may be covered by a site-wide agreement; never classify it as excluded solely because the asset list is incomplete.
